title: Getting through the office door
target: How the keycard door in R.E.P.O. works and how items that switch, light up or unlock behave once you are through it.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A level with the shop's keycard door
A crew that can share what is behind it

steps.do: Expect the office door to be a locked and an unlocked state rather than a key you hold.
steps.because: the keycard is kept in a locked and an unlocked state (shop office keycard_LOCKED, shop office keycard_UNLOCKED)

steps.do: Look for the door that belongs to the shop rather than any door.
steps.because: the shop has a keycard door of its own (ShopKeycardDoor)

steps.do: Read the panel rather than the handle: it is where the door answers you.
steps.because: the door has its own panel, switches material when it opens and carries an unlock sound (shopKeycardPanelMeshRenderer, unlockedMaterial, unlockSound)

steps.do: Treat it as a physical door, because it is hung rather than a way of moving a player.
steps.because: it is a hinged physical object with a level collider (hingedPhysGrabObject, levelColliderObject)

steps.do: Expect items to keep a state of their own once you are through.
steps.because: items have a state of their own with a manager behind them (ItemState, ItemManager, ItemAttributes)

steps.do: Toggle deliberately and check whether it turns itself off when put away.
steps.because: an item can be toggled, with a toggle state, a sound and a rule about switching off when put away (ItemToggle, toggleState, playSound, autoTurnOffWhenEquipped, onToggle)

steps.do: Know whether a carried light is meant to stay on.
steps.because: an item can carry a light with an intensity curve and a setting for staying on (ItemLight, itemLight, lightIntensityCurve, alwaysActive)

steps.do: Watch how loud a tool is, because it has its own level.
steps.because: an item carries a sound level of its own, with types including one for items from the secret shop (ItemVolume, itemVolume, volumes, itemSecretShopType)

commonMistakes: Hunting for a key item when the door answers to a locked and unlocked state.
Yanking the door instead of using its panel.
Leaving a tool switched on and putting it away.
Carrying a light that was never set to stay on.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
